intent.raw: Leave track and game features for later. Make login, auth, and Strava connection possible first. Use validation/poker-team as auth reference, learn from Savvy browser cookie session/security definitions, and shape a reusable auth/user-management project that can be copied into later projects.
intent.objective: Refine a reusable auth/user-management foundation and Body War first-consumer Strava connection into a production-ready non-executed plan.
intent.operator_sentence: auth/user-management first, Body War Strava connection next, track and game later

route_menu.context_hint: The operator wants a portable auth/user-management foundation, not a one-off Body War game implementation.

items.label: Reusable auth foundation first
items.description: Design auth/user-management as its own copyable project and make Body War the first consumer for Strava connection.

items.label: Body War direct auth
items.description: Implement login and Strava directly in Body War, then extract reusable pieces later.

items.label: Full game MVP
items.description: Continue the broader track, scoring, and game implementation plan before auth extraction.

technique_overlays.trigger: Refine requires the canonical ten-stage loop before a final synthesis or next-route recommendation.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every non-first step consumes a prior frame, handle, decision, ledger, artifact, or external context; stage receipts stay grouped by dispatch id.

technique_overlays.trigger: The target could be implemented directly in Body War, extracted later, or designed first as a reusable auth/user-management foundation.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The selected route keeps reusable auth as the first artifact boundary and records confirmation before execution.

technique_overlays.trigger: Auth/user-management hides multiple components: identity, session, token, permission, resource, provider link, Strava OAuth, storage, browser safety, and audit.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The design output must describe each component by owner, context, contract, evidence, and what transfers to later projects.

technique_overlays.trigger: The route references private submodules, auth/session details, OAuth tokens, browser cookies, and Strava account-linking context.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Private evidence remains local-path evidence; no token, secret, or private validation content is copied into public surfaces.

technique_overlays.trigger: Prior Body War and Savvy runs already contain Strava blockers, auth findings, and session-guard evidence that must be reused without drifting into stale authority.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Prior memory is used as routing context only; final claims must cite current local files or be marked as residue.

subagent_strategy.trigger: Production-ready reusable auth spans domain auth, browser session security, and Strava OAuth provider integration; independent lanes reduce false transfer from poker-team or Savvy into the new foundation.
subagent_strategy.explanation: Run three read-only sibling reviews after confirmation. The parent refine run owns final synthesis, decisions, and next-route recommendation.
context: Auth domain reference: validation/poker-team/docs/features/auth-access-control and backend auth use cases
First consumer: projects/body-war login plus Strava connection
Deferred: track geometry and game mechanics

roles.purpose: Map poker-team auth-access-control into reusable auth concepts while excluding poker-specific roles, permissions, and product assumptions.
roles.owns: auth domain, session, token, permission, login/logout/introspection, and deny-by-default transfer rules

roles.purpose: Review cookie session, CSRF, server session store, localStorage avoidance, resource scope, and browser guard risks using Savvy as evidence.
roles.owns: browser session transport and threat-model acceptance gates

roles.purpose: Define Strava OAuth provider-link scope, state validation, token custody, refresh/revocation, redacted audit, and first-consumer Body War handoff.
roles.owns: Strava provider adapter and Body War consumer boundary

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Confirm permission to run the auth-user-management refine strategy with three delegated read-only lanes: auth-domain-porter, browser-session-security, and strava-provider-integration?

gates.condition: Approval checkpoint: operator confirms runtime-backed stages and delegated read-only subagent execution.
Private poker-team, Savvy, and Body War evidence may be cited by local path but must not be copied into public Arcanum surfaces or exported with secrets.
Each runtime-backed stage records a native stage receipt or explicit blocked reason before final synthesis.
The refine run produces a non-executed plan only; Body War, Savvy, and poker-team runtime code remain read-only.
Production-ready means the plan names acceptance gates for auth, session, provider-link, Strava token custody, audit, tests, deployment, and adoption docs; it does not claim implementation proof.

boundaries.contract: Reference local evidence by path; do not mutate or copy private source packages during refine.
Body War consumes a login plus Strava connection adapter after the reusable auth core is defined; track and game work stays deferred.
No real OAuth client secrets, callback secrets, refresh tokens, or athlete data enter repository artifacts.

authority.lifecycle: Refine owns the strategy packet and final synthesis.
authority.execution: Task Session or later implementation routes own code changes.
authority.evidence: Poker-team, Savvy, and Body War own their source evidence.
authority.memory: Memory may route the run but current local files must support final claims.
authority.promotion: No canonical promotion is performed by this refine run.

state_namespaces.write_policy: Refine artifacts and Craft ledger may be written; runtime code is not created during strategy preparation.
Only planning links may be updated during strategy preparation; app code remains read-only.

promotion_guardrails: Do not treat route validation as implementation evidence.
Do not claim production-ready implementation before task-session receipts exist.
Do not copy private validation or project evidence into public Arcanum surfaces.
Do not expand the first implementation slice into track geometry or game mechanics.
